Article Title: 'Entire country must unite': CJP's Dipke backs INDIA bloc protest, calls for more demonstrations against CEC
Article Text:
File photo: CJP backs INDIA bloc's SC march, says protests will continue till CEC resigns

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday backed the INDIA bloc’s protest march to the Supreme Court, saying demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would continue across the country until he resigned.Dipke welcomed Monday’s INDIA bloc protest in Delhi, describing it as a “very large and important protest” and calling for more such demonstrations across the country.“It is necessary for the entire country to unite and hold such protests, especially the INDIA bloc, as it is in the opposition,” he said.“Such protests will continue across the country until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. We hope that this happens,” Dipke added.Reacting to the Congress Kerala unit’s now-deleted social media post demanding Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s resignation over his remarks that law and order was not the Supreme Court’s responsibility, Dipke said he did not want to comment on the controversy at this stage.Dipke, however, questioned the Supreme Court’s response to alleged irregularities involving the Election Commission, asking what action the court had taken against the poll body.“What action have they taken against the Election Commission? They have taken no action at all,” he said, referring to the court’s recent remarks on the issue.Citing the deletion of voters’ names in West Bengal, Dipke questioned the reasoning that those unable to vote could do so in a subsequent election.“Will the Supreme Court tell Narendra Modi the same thing, that he should not contest the election this time and can contest the next time? If they cannot say that, then on what basis are they telling voters this?” he asked.The remarks came amid a political row over the Congress Kerala unit’s post targeting the CJI. The post, which was later deleted, said: “Dear Surya Kant, if law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it.”The BJP criticised the Congress over the post, accusing it of attacking constitutional institutions. Union minister Kiren Rijiju said that while protest was every citizen’s right, “brazenly abusing” constitutional authorities was deplorable.BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi accused the Congress of seeking to create anarchy by undermining constitutional institutions. He also criticised the INDIA bloc’s march to the Supreme Court, alleging that the opposition was attempting to influence or intimidate the judiciary.Earlier, CJI Surya Kant had said that law and order was not his domain when asked about the restrictions imposed amid anti-CEC protests in Delhi. He also said the Supreme Court’s doors remained open to everyone, including ordinary citizens and lawmakers.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) founder Abhijeet Dipke backed the INDIA bloc’s protest march to the Supreme Court. He said demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would continue across the country until he resigned.

Article Title: Students union body NSUI stages flash protest at Rajiv Chowk metro station, several detained
Article Text:
Security personnel detain National Students' Union of India (NSUI)

NEW DELHI: Several members of the Congress-affiliated National Students' Union of India (NSUI) were detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday after staging a flash protest outside Gate 7 of Rajiv Chowk metro station, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities.The protesters gathered at the busy metro station in Connaught Place, raising allegations of "vote chori" and seeking accountability from the Election Commission."NSUI's fight against vote chori will continue with full force until Gyanesh Kumar resigns," said the organisation's national media in-charge, Ravi Pandey.The demonstration followed another round of police action earlier in the day, when Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained after arriving at Jantar Mantar, where heavy barricading and security arrangements had been put in place.The protests come a day after Delhi Police de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, amid growing demands from protesters for the CEC's resignation. A march was organised by INDIA bloc leaders and supporters, led by Rahul Gandhi, along Barakhamba Road towards the Supreme Court on Monday. Subsequently, 11 opposition leaders moved the apex court, challenging the Election Commission's decisions related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Several members of Congress-affiliated National Students' Union of India (NSUI) detained by Delhi Police. Demonstration followed another round of police action earlier in the day. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained at Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: ‘Biggest red flag’: BJP targets Rahul Gandhi over CEC row, alleges track record of bribery
Article Text:
Union Minister Piyush Goyal addresses a press conference

BJP 's big bribery charge

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday launched a sharp attack on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the opposition’s protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission of India ’s (ECI). The party accused the Congress of double standards while citing the grand-old-party's "record".Union minister Piyush Goyal in a press conference said that Congress is in 'delulu is the solulu' mode, while describing Rahul Gandhi as a 'red flag' for his party. The minister questioned the Congress’s record on election commissioners and its objections to the electoral roll revision exercise."For the past few days, we have been seeing the conduct and double standards of Rahul Gandhi, seeing his childish actions which demolish every aspect of the Constitution," the minister said.“Congress questions the fairness of Election Commission but overlooks its own track record,” Goyal added.Defending the government amid row over CEC, Goyal said the NDA government has allowed the EC to function independently and has not offered political positions to commissioners in exchange for their services.He alleged that the Congress had appointed former chief election commissioners to political positions after their tenures, citing former CECs TN Seshan and MS Gill, among others.Goyal referred to Seshan’s candidature on a Congress ticket in the 1999 Lok Sabha election against BJP veteran LK Advani, asking whether the move amounted to rewarding a former election commissioner.He also questioned the Padma Vibhushan conferred on Gill in 2000, "MS Gill served as Chief Election Commissioner for five years, from 1996 to 2001. Interestingly, he was awarded the Padma Vibhushan. In 2000, while he was still the sitting Chief Election Commissioner, he was conferred India's second-highest civilian honour. Was this not an inducement? Was it not, in effect, a form of bribery?"The minister also highlighted the 2023 law introduced by the Modi government governing the appointment of election commissioners. Under the new framework, the selection committee includes the prime minister, a Union cabinet minister nominated by the prime minister and the leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha.Goyal’s remarks come amid opposition protests against SIR and allegations of electoral irregularities. The Congress and other INDIA bloc parties have challenged aspects of the exercise, arguing that the process raises concerns about electoral rights and the integrity of voter lists.Goyal also questioned Rahul Gandhi over the Congress’s objections to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, asking why the party had not raised similar concerns when the exercise was conducted in Bihar, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. “Where was the Congress at that time?” he asked.He also questioned the party’s opposition to removing duplicate voter entries, citing public remarks by senior Congress leaders about duplicate names on electoral rolls. If the Congress believes elections are rigged, the Election Commission is not functioning properly and SIR is flawed, Goyal asked whether Congress chief ministers should resign in states governed by the party.
Article Summary: Union minister Piyush Goyal in a press conference said that Congress is in 'delulu is the solulu' mode, while describing Rahul Gandhi as a'red flag' for his party. The minister questioned the Congress’s record on election commissioners and its objections to the electoral roll revision exercise.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi, INDIA bloc's plea against EC still not listed yet as 14 defects remain

The registry had pointed out 14 defects in the petition

NEW DELHI: The petition filed by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 10 other opposition leaders against the Election Commission of India (ECI) was not listed for hearing in the Supreme Court on Tuesday as defects flagged by the registry remain to be rectified, news agency PTI reported.According to the Supreme Court website, the registry had pointed out 14 defects in the petition, including the absence of a clear copy of the identity card of Congress president and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, who is among the petitioners. The registry also flagged illegible or missing pages in the documents submitted.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut, who is also a petitioner, acknowledged the discrepancies on Tuesday and said the opposition would rectify them. Speaking to ANI, Raut said the petition had a shortfall of Rs 220 in the filing fee and referred to errors involving 14 documents.“There might be some errors in it, which we will now rectify and repair,” Raut said, adding that the leaders who participated in Monday's protest were petitioners in the legal challenge.The INDIA bloc leaders approached the Supreme Court following their march against the ECI on October 12, demanding accountability from the poll body over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Raut said the opposition wanted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign and sought the restoration of names allegedly deleted from electoral rolls. He also accused the government of exerting political pressure on the ECI.On the opposition's next course of action, Raut said Rahul Gandhi had invited the leaders for tea on Tuesday evening, after which they would decide their future direction. He added that the leaders would remain in Delhi until the next steps were finalised.
Article Summary: The registry had pointed out 14 defects in the petition. The registry also flagged illegible or missing pages in the documents submitted. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut, who is also a petitioner, acknowledged the discrepancies on Tuesday and said the opposition would rectify them.

Article Title: 'Congress will push him out as CM': Kumaraswamy after DKS being 'pushed' at Delhi march
Article Text:
Kumaraswamy said recent political developments in Karnataka were creating an “extremely bad political culture”.

NEW DELHI: Union minister HD Kumaraswamy on Tuesday attacked the Congress party and Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar over an incident during the INDIA bloc's protest march in Delhi, warning that soon he "will be pushed out from CM post."Speaking to the media, Kumaraswamy said he was raising the issue with pain and would not comment further on Monday’s incident, in which Shivakumar was allegedly pulled back by security personnel during the march. However, he suggested that the episode could have wider political implications.“It is just the beginning, Congress will eventually push him out from CM post,” Kumaraswamy said, adding that “the day is not far when even his chair will be pulled away.”The remarks came after the BJP shared a video circulating online that appeared to show Congress leader Rahul Gandhi pulling Shivakumar by the collar as the two marched towards the Supreme Court to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Moments later, Shivakumar appeared to be pulled back as the Congress MP moves forward with the crowd.Kumaraswamy also said that said recent political developments in Karnataka were creating an “extremely bad political culture” that needed to end.He said the state was grappling with several pressing issues, including farmers’ demand for a scientifically determined price for sugarcane, drought conditions, and matters concerning the Bidadi township and the NICE project.However, he alleged that the controversy surrounding a sting operation had overshadowed these concerns after the chief minister raised the issue at a Cabinet meeting.Kumaraswamy also questioned Shivakumar’s alleged appointment of four retired police officers at his Sadashivanagar residence, claiming they had been tasked with gathering information about discussions among ministers.“Earlier, he had appointed only journalists to gather information for his office. Now, he has appointed four police officers to gather information about what is being discussed by ministers in his Cabinet. This discussion has begun within the police department,” Kumaraswamy claimed.On the sting operation case, he said the Nija Horata Samiti had filed a complaint in court and that an investigation was underway. He also alleged that a former chief minister had obtained a stay from the court in the matter.Kumaraswamy accused Shivakumar of initiating the sting operation controversy and said he should now face its consequences.“Mr Shivakumar, you were the one who initiated the sting operation. You nurtured it and allowed it to grow into a major controversy. Now you must face the consequences,” he said.Kumaraswamy also referred to the Prajwal Revanna case, alleging that videos were circulated on pen drives in Mandya and Hassan just four days before polling during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.He claimed that a recorded conversation and an audio clip involving a lawyer and others pointed to an alleged conspiracy to tarnish the Deve Gowda family. He also alleged that Shivakumar had spoken about getting complaints filed through women and the circulation of videos.Kumaraswamy further referred to the Ramesh Jarkiholi case, alleging that a conspiracy had been hatched against him. These claims were not independently established in the information provided.He urged Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah to speak out on the controversy and call for an inquiry. Referring to Siddaramaiah as his political teacher and a leader who had fought for the AHINDA community, Kumaraswamy said the chief minister should help establish the truth.“I don't say he should destabilise the government, but it is his teacher who fought for the AHINDA community from the political beginning. He should speak about these issues and bring out what is the truth and a CBI enquiry must be done,” he said.Kumaraswamy stressed that the controversy could damage the state’s reputation beyond the individuals involved.“It is not about one person or one family. These things will destroy the family culture in Karnataka and these kind of sting operations can bring very bad name to the whole state,” he said.“That is why I am demanding an enquiry that has to be done on the proposal of Chief Minister DK Shivakumar in Karnataka. I am also meeting Union Home Minister Amit Shah in the upcoming days to request the same,” he added.Kumaraswamy argued that approaching the court did not resolve the underlying issues and called for an inquiry into the alleged sting operations.He also criticised the Special Investigation Team (SIT) that investigated the Prajwal Revanna case, questioning its role and accusing it of remaining silent to protect certain people.“I’m asking, where is that SIT team, which did all these blenders in Karnataka and now keeping quite to safeguard some people with Distrupting agenda,” he said.Kumaraswamy added that he had not raised these issues when HD Revanna and his family were targeted and Prajwal Revanna was jailed following the SIT investigation.
Article Summary: HD Kumaraswamy attacked the Congress party and Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar over an incident during the INDIA bloc's protest march in Delhi. He said he was raising the issue with pain and would not comment further on Monday’s incident. The remarks came after the BJP shared a video circulating online that appeared to show Congress leader Rahul Gandhi.

Article Title: Missing pages, Rs 200 fee shortfall: SC flags 14 defects in INDIA bloc plea against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
SC flags over 10 defects in Rahul's plea against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court registry Monday flagged 14 defects in a petition filed by the Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the special intensive revision of electoral rolls.The registry asked the lawyer who filed the petition to submit a clear copy of the identity card of Congress chief and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge , one of the co-petitioners, news agency PTI reported.The registry also flagged illegible or missing pages in the petition. It further pointed out a shortfall of Rs 220 in the court fee.Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut responded to the Supreme Court registry flagging defects in the opposition bloc's petition, saying the INDIA bloc remained determined to hold the constitutional body accountable.Speaking to news agency ANI about the technical discrepancies in the petition, Raut said, "The petition that has been filed mentions that the fee is short by Rs 220, there are several errors, and there are facts about 14 documents mentioned in it. Well, it is possible. We have individual petitions in the names of Rahul Ji, Mallikarjun Kharge Ji, and all other India Bloc leaders. There might be some errors in it, which we will now rectify and repair.Confirming his participation in the legal challenge, Raut said, "Definitely, I am a petitioner. All the parties that were involved in yesterday's protest are all petitioners."On Monday, Rahul and several other opposition leaders marched to the Supreme Court to file the petition.The INDIA bloc leaders, led by Rahul Gandhi and joined by thousands of supporters, sought scrutiny of the Election Commission 's functioning, measures to prevent CEC Gyanesh Kumar from taking decisions "unilaterally", alleged "arbitrary" voter deletions during SIR, and the system governing the use and deployment of electronic voting machines (EVMs).The petitioners included Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, TMC's Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav, RJD's Tejashwi Yadav, Sena (UBT)'s Sanjay Raut, CPM's M A Baby, CPI's D Raja, JMM's Mahua Majhi, NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule and IUML's E T Mohammed Basheer.The opposition leaders sought a suspension of SIR without challenging its legality. They also called for eligible voters to be included in the electoral rolls of Punjab and other poll-bound states.After the CJI declined to meet the opposition delegation, Rahul said, "We respect CJI and SC. We are quite happy he has given us a path forward. To tell us we can file a petition is a path forward."The petition also sought the formation of an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge and assisted by technical experts and other eminent citizens. The panel would be tasked with conducting an independent audit, within a fixed timeframe, of deletions and changes made to electoral rolls during SIR.The plea further requested the court to set up a panel to "examine integrity of electoral-roll databases and SIR rollout".
Article Summary: SC flags over 10 defects in Rahul's plea against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut responded to the Supreme Court registry flagging defects in the opposition bloc's petition. Rahul said, "We respect CJI and SC. We are quite happy he has given us a path forward"

She questioned the timeline of the incident and the journalist’s subsequent hospital visit. She also raised questions about an X-ray reportedly being conducted despite Parashar saying she was pregnant.Other Congress leaders and supporters shared videos of the commotion, arguing that the footage did not clearly show Rahul pushing Parashar.The incident took place during the INDIA bloc’s march to the Supreme Court over allegations concerning electoral rolls and CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

Article Title: SC stays criminal defamation trial against Rahul Gandhi in ‘Chowkidar chor hai’ case
Article Text:
SC stays defamation trial against Rahul Gandhi over remarks against PM Modi

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday stayed trial court proceedings against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi in a criminal defamation case over his alleged ‘Chowkidar chor hai’ remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi.The court also issued a notice on Rahul's plea challenging the Bombay high court’s order refusing to quash the defamation case."Issue notice returnable in four weeks. Further proceedings before the trial court shall remain stayed," news agency PTI quoted the bench saying.Senior advocate Abhishek Singhvi, appearing for Rahul, cited earlier Supreme Court judgments and argued that the law on the matter was settled. The bench posted the case for further hearing after four weeks.The Bombay HC, on September 8, refused to quash the summons issued to Rahul in 2019, dismissing his challenge to a Girgaum magistrate’s order dated August 28, 2019.However, it extended its 2021 order directing the magistrate to defer proceedings for six weeks to allow the Congress leader to approach the Supreme Court.The complaint was filed by BJP worker Mahesh Shrishrimal over Rahul's speech in Rajasthan on September 20, 2018. Shrishrimal argued that, as a BJP member, he was aggrieved by remarks against the party’s leader.The complaint alleged that Rahul's statements defamed PM Modi and amounted to allegations against BJP members and Indian citizens associated with him.
Article Summary: The court also issued a notice on Rahul's plea challenging the Bombay high court’s order refusing to quash the defamation case. The bench posted the case for further hearing after four weeks. The complaint was filed by BJP worker Mahesh Shrishrimal over Rahul's speech in Rajasthan.

Article Title: INDIA bloc files petition in SC on SIR voter deletions

NEW DELHI: Opposition INDIA bloc members, led by leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and joined by thousands of supporters, undertook their march to Supreme Court on Monday to file a joint petition seeking intense scrutiny into a host of issues - functioning of EC, preventing CEC Gyanesh Kumar from taking decisions "unilaterally", "arbitrary" deletion of voters during SIR, and the architecture governing use and deployment of EVMs.Rahul and other petitioners - Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, TMC's Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav, RJD's Tejashwi Yadav, Sena (UBT)'s Sanjay Raut, CPM's M A Baby, CPI's D Raja, JMM's Mahua Majhi, NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule and IUML's E T Mohammed Basheer - sought suspension of SIR without questioning its legality, and, inclusion of eligible voters in rolls of Punjab and other poll-bound states.On CJI's refusal to meet the opposition delegation, Rahul said, "We respect CJI and SC. We are quite happy he has given us a path forward. To tell us we can file a petition is a path forward." The petition requested the court to set up a panel led by a retired SC judge, comprising technical experts and persons of eminence to "examine integrity of electoral-roll databases and SIR rollout".The petitioners also wanted the panel to ‘review processes, procedures, protocols and technical architecture governing EVMs’.They said, “The validity of SIR does not dispense with the requirement that each decision taken in its implementation must conform to Constitution, governing statutes and applicable rules.”The present plea is instituted in the larger public interest of safeguarding the constitutional right of every eligible citizen to vote, maintaining institutional independence and collective functioning of EC, and ensuring that the preparation and revision of poll rolls are carried out transparently, lawfully and in a manner that inspires public confidence in the democratic process, the opposition functionaries argued.Flagging alleged unlawful modification of Form 6, used for enrolment of new voters, the petitioners, through advocate Prasanna S, said, “Addition of an unauthorised condition to a statutory form may impose an unlawful burden upon eligible citizens seeking registration, particularly first-time voters, and may result in the exclusion of persons otherwise entitled to be enrolled.”The SC registry pointed out several defects in the petition, and the counsel said he will cure them in due course.The opposition members also objected to centralised and opaque functioning of ECINET and ERONET poll rolls database and the “large-scale exclusion of voters without adequate notice, hearing or an effective mechanism for restoration in case of wrongful or erroneous deletions”.Invoking fundamental rights of people under Articles 14, 19, 21 read with Article 324 (EC) of the Constitution, they sought a direction from SC to EC to produce in court “complete files, agendas, minutes, file noting and objections recorded by election commissioners in respect of each of the disputed decisions related to SIR, together with relevant ECINET and ERONET access logs and complete file recording on EC’s June 24, 2025 decision to commence SIR across the country”.Pending decision on the petition, they said EC must function as per the mandate of the Constitution in a democratic manner and ensure Form 6 conformed to Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.They wanted EC to “publish, booth-wise, the names of all electors deleted during the SIR, together with the reasons for each deletion and a breakdown of deletions by gender and age, and to provide an effective and functional mechanism for restoring the names of electors found eligible for inclusion in the poll rolls”.

NEW DELHI: In a relief to Punjab govt, Supreme Court Monday directed that no coercive steps be taken by the CBI in a case registered in connection with corruption allegations linked to the office of Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann A bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale, however, said that it was not staying the FIR registered in the case and issued notice to the CBI on the petition filed by govt challenging the HC's direction to register the case. Article Title: 4 new governors named, picks underline BJP focus on elections
Article Text: NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu on Monday appointed four new governors - Sudha Yadav of Karnataka, Dhal Singh Bisen of Uttarakhand, Dushyant Gautam of Sikkim and Braj Mohan Ram of Odisha.While Yadav, who hails from Haryana, and Bisen, who is from the agriculturist Bhoyar Pawar caste from MP, belong to the OBC category, both Gautam (Jatav) and Ram (Dhobi) are from SC community, underlining BJP's focus on two demographics which are crucial voting segments in many states, including in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh.Yadav, also a member of BJP parliamentary board, entered politics after her husband, BSF deputy commandant Sukhbir Yadav, was killed in the 1999 Kargil War.The other three appointees are former BJP MPs.The preference for Dalits and OBCs is in line with party's push since 2014 to consolidate the support it has gained among communities which were not part of its core base until PM Narendra Modi's emergence as its mascot. The choices come before assembly elections in party's strongholds of UP and Uttarakhand. Early on, party had fielded a diverse slate of candidates for Rajya Sabha polls from UP, with the coveted berths going to, apart from upper castes, OBCs and SCs.Meanwhile, according to an official communication, Keralam governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar was shifted to Tamil Nadu, and Sikkim's Om Prakash Mathur will take charge in Keralam.
Article Summary: Sudha Yadav of Karnataka, Dhal Singh Bisen of Uttarakhand, Dushyant Gautam of Sikkim and Braj Mohan Ram of Odisha appointed as governors. By 1.30 pm, Barakhamba Road, which was closed to traffic, was full of opposition supporters and protesters. Some climbed onto buses and waved their flags above the crowd while waiting for Rahul and other alliance members.Around 3.30 pm, Rahul arrived with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other members of the alliance in a bus, which first approached Barakhamba Road from the Mandi House side, took a U-turn near Statesman House and headed back towards Mandi House as supporters marched in solidarity.Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee visited Constitution Club to express “solidarity” before leaving for Kolkata.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and SP chief Akhilesh Yadav were among those present. The bus also carried K C Venugopal, Tejashwi Yadav, Supriya Sule, Dipankar Bhattacharya, Sanjay Raut, MA Baby, D Raja, DK Shivakumar, Revanth Reddy, Dharmendra Yadav, Sachin Pilot, Abhishek Singhvi, Saugata Roy, V Sivadasan and Deepender Hooda, along with Yogendra Yadav, Neha Bora and Sai Balaji.Rahul, Priyanka and Bora then got off the bus and began walking together, with thousands following. Members of student organisations and civil society groups as well as youth activists joined opposition supporters, their cheers accompanying the march towards Supreme Court.” echoed along the stretch. Another chant, “”, seemed to target PM Modi, home minister Amit Shah and the CEC. Some turned up wearing Batman masks, referencing a viral meme depicting Rahul as the superhero.The procession had travelled only a short distance when police stopped it. Near Barakhamba Road, demonstrators pushed through barricades as cops tried to push them back. Rahul was subsequently seen atop a truck with Akhilesh, Tejashwi, Venugopal and Sule, among others.On Bhagwan Das Road, many climbed onto a line of parked police vehicles and buses, shouting and cheering as the INDIA bloc members waved back at them. Flags of NSUI, Youth Congress, AISA, AISF and SP fluttered above the crowd.Police then began directing the supporters to one side. People started pushing and pulling as security personnel — officers said more than 10,000 personnel had been deployed in and around New Delhi — moved into the crowd.Amid this, the truck carrying the politicians took a U-turn and headed in the opposite direction, while the protesters began scattering. Later, the politicians reached Supreme Court and a petition was filed naming Election Commission of India as a respondent. The plea challenges the decisions taken related to the SIR of electoral rolls and calls for transparency and safeguards against voter deletions.The march followed CJI Surya Kant’s decision to decline a meeting sought by opposition members to submit a memorandum on alleged electoral irregularities. Citing proceedings already pending before the court, he advised them to raise their concerns through a formal petition.Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee president Devender Yadav said, “As long as this vote thief (CEC Kumar) does not step down, this movement will continue”. He added, “We have been fighting this battle for a long time. But BJP has been protecting the CEC as he acts at the behest of Modi and Shah to indulge in malpractices to steal elections by robbing people’s verdict. From now on, he won’t be allowed to misuse his position. He has committed anti-national and anti-people sins from which he cannot escape. He will be made to pay for his crimes through this people’s movement.”
Article Summary: Opposition supporters turned roads between Connaught Place and Supreme Court into a sea of supporters waving flags and shouting slogans. The alliance was demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and a halt to the SIR of electoral rolls over allegations of irregularities.

Article Title: Will hit streets again until PM Modi’s dictatorship ends, says CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke
Article Text:
Abhijeet also alleged that the police subjected him to mental harassment at a time when his grandmother had died.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday said his agitation would continue until what he called Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “dictatorship” came to an end.Speaking to the reporters following his recent arrest, Dipke accused the Delhi Police of mentally harassing him, violating his fundamental rights and preventing him from contacting his lawyer and family.“We will continue our agitation until Narendra Modi’s dictatorship ends. We will soon return to the streets,” Dipke said, reiterating his resolve to continue the protest despite the police action.Dipke’s mother, Anita, said the family would never forget how the govt’s actions prevented her son from seeing his grandmother for the last time. “We will not forget this until our last breath. Because of this govt, Abhijeet could not see his grandmother for the last time,” she said.Abhijeet alleged that Delhi Police violated his legal rights during his arrest by denying him access to his lawyer and brother. He challenged police to release the complete, unedited video of the arrest, claiming authorities withheld his whereabouts and details of the police station where he was detained from his family and legal representatives for an entire day.Abhijeet also alleged that the police subjected him to mental harassment at a time when his grandmother had died. “At around 3.30am, the police brought the arrest papers to me and pressured me to sign them, saying that I would be in jail for a long time and should call my parents and inform them,” he claimed, describing the episode as mental harassment of both him and his family.He also criticised the police for allegedly deploying women personnel during the arrest. Claiming that the move was intended to protect male officers from allegations of misconduct, Dipke said he and his associates were educated and knew how to treat women with respect. His allegations against Delhi Police could not be independently verified.Responding to questions about the possibility of externment from Maharashtra, Dipke targeted chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , questioning the state govt’s intentions and its handling of the issue.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday said his agitation would continue until what he called Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s ‘dictatorship’ came to an end. Dipke accused the Delhi Police of mentally harassing him, preventing him from contacting his lawyer and family.

Article Title: Actor Imran Khan’s CJP protest participation under lens over 'OCI rules violation'

BJP’s Kirit Somaiya, who had flagged the alleged violation, said Khan is mentioned in a general FIR





MUMBAI: Police are in the process of writing to immigration officials over allegations that actor Imran Khan holds an overseas citizen of India card and had violated rules by participating in CJP’s stir on Saturday, said senior Gamdevi police inspector Prashant Mohite.BJP’s Kirit Somaiya, who had flagged the alleged violation, said Khan is mentioned in a general FIR but a separate case needs to be filed against him.He said he will visit the police station on Monday to ensure a separate FIR is lodged.

Article Title: Hyderabad woman stabbed to death by husband during argument
Article Text:
A 32-year-old woman named Ajmira Begum was killed by her husband Mustafa in Balapur.





HYDERABAD: A 32-year-old woman was killed by her husband in Balapur on Monday night. Police said that Ajmira Begum died after she was attacked with a knife.Her husband Mustafa is at large. He is a native of West Bengal who migrated to Hyderabad and is residing with his wife and children in Balapur.The relationship between the couple got strained and it was in this connection that they had an argument on Monday night.During the argument, he picked up a nearby knife and attacked her.Following the murder, he fled from the police.Police registered a case of murder and are on the lookout for the accused.
Article Summary: Police said that Ajmira Begum died after she was attacked with a knife. Her husband Mustafa is at large. He is a native of West Bengal who migrated to Hyderabad and is residing with his wife and children in Balapur.

Article Title: Kargil War widow and BJP veteran Sudha Yadav is new Karnataka governor
Article Text:
In Aug 2022, Sudha Yadav was inducted into the BJP's Parliamentary Board, its highest decision-making body.





BENGALURU: With incumbent Thaawar Chand Gehlot completing five years in office, President Droupadi Murmu on Monday appointed Kargil War widow and BJP leader Sudha Yadav, 61, next governor of Karnataka.Yadav, a former MP and member of BJP's Parliamentary Board, will be the state's second woman governor after VS Ramadevi, who held office from Dec 1999 to Aug 2002.Yadav holds a doctorate in chemistry from Roorkee University, now IIT-Roorkee. She entered politics after her husband, BSF deputy commandant Sukhbir Singh Yadav, was killed during the 1999 Kargil War.BJP fielded her from Mahendragarh in Haryana in 1999 Lok Sabha elections, which she won. She represented the constituency until 2004.She subsequently served as BJP national secretary and headed its OBC Morcha.She was a member of National Commission for Backward Classes from 2019 to 2022.In Aug 2022, she was inducted into the BJP's Parliamentary Board, its highest decision-making body.
Article Summary: Yadav will be the state's second woman governor after VS Ramadevi, who held office from Dec 1999 to Aug 2002. She entered politics after her husband, BSF deputy commandant Sukhbir Singh Yadav, was killed during the 1999 Kargil War.

Article Title: 'PM Modi's problem is not with Jantar Mantar as a location, but with protests': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke
Article Text:
“You cannot denotify the resistance, Narendra Modi,” Dipke said in the post.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday said protests would continue across the country until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigned, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was afraid of public protests.Reacting to the de-notification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, Dipke said the move would not stop demonstrations, but lead to similar protest sites emerging across the country."Narendra Modi's fear is evident from the fact that he has removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. He thinks protests will stop if Jantar Mantar is no longer a designated protest site, but that is not going to happen. Jantar Mantars will now emerge across the country," Dipke said."Narendra Modi's problem is not with Jantar Mantar as a location, but with protests. We must understand this," he added.Meanwhile, Delhi Police detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on Tuesday as they attempted to reach Jantar Mantar, police said.In a post on X, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke claimed that several other team members, including Ajinkya Shinde, had also been detained."Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police," Dipke said.“You cannot denotify the resistance, Narendra Modi,” Dipke said in the post.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday said protests would continue across the country until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigned. “You cannot denotify the resistance, Narendra Modi,” Dipke said in the post.

Article Title: Watch: CJP’s Saurav Das records video from detention bus after trying to enter Jantar Mantar
Article Text:
CJP’s Saurav Das shares video from detention bus

‘Jantar Mantar is a designated protest site’: CJP leader

CJP leaders detained

Jantar Mantar removed from list of designated protest sites





NEW DELHI: “Jantar Mantar has been breached. We were inside and now they are detaining us and taking us away,” Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das said in a video shared on Instagram on Tuesday, claiming that party members had entered the protest site before being detained by Delhi Police The video, apparently recorded from inside a detention bus, shows footage from outside Jantar Mantar as Das addresses supporters and raises slogans alongside other detained members.In the video, Das says the group has entered Jantar Mantar and is being taken away by police. He then turns the camera towards the scenes outside before urging supporters to continue the campaign.In the video, Das reiterates the party’s stand on the protest venue, while CJP leader Ashutosh Ranka says the demonstration will continue until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns.“Jantar Mantar is a designated protest site. And we will get the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar from Jantar Mantar,” Ranka says in the footage.The video ends with slogans of “Bharat Mata ki Jai” and “Jai Bhim” as the police action continues.Delhi Police detained CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das, national spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka and team member Ajinkya Shinde on Tuesday while they were attempting to enter Jantar Mantar, police sources said.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke also claimed that several other members carrying the national flag had entered the venue before being detained.In a post on X, Dipke said, “You cannot denotify the resistance,” after sharing a video that purportedly showed party members jumping over a gate to enter the site and raising slogans.The detentions came after Delhi Police de-notified Jantar Mantar as a protest venue on October 11. The decision followed recommendations by a Union home ministry committee tasked with identifying suitable locations for demonstrations.Police designated Ramlila Maidan in central Delhi, Burari Ground in north Delhi and CBD Ground in Shahdara as alternative protest venues.The change came after the Supreme Court asked authorities to identify a suitable alternative site with basic facilities for protesters.The CJP has been demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The party has maintained that it will continue its campaign despite the denial of permission for its proposed demonstration.(With agency inputs)

Article Title: Masked men tie up BJP leader Ramesh Yadav, loot Rs 50 lakh at Kanpur farmhouse
Article Text:
The farmhouse, spread across four bighas, has 50 CCTV cameras.





KANPUR: BJP Pichhda Morcha state minister Ramesh Yadav was robbed of Rs 50 lakh after masked men tied his hands and legs at his farmhouse in Kanpur around midnight on Monday.The incident occurred at Nyori in the Sen Paschimpara police station area, 20 kilometres from the city. Police were informed at 1.20 am.Yadav, who became BJP Pichhda Morcha state minister on Oct 1, had returned to Kanpur at 12.30 am after assuming charge in Lucknow on Monday.He was alone at the farmhouse, 500 metres from his house, although four guards were deployed there.Joint police commissioner Vipin Tada and DCP Deependranath Chaudhary reached the spot with police personnel.Investigators found no CCTV footage showing the intruders entering the farmhouse.However, two men wearing black clothes were caught on camera while fleeing. They stepped on a washbasin and jumped over a tin shed to escape.The farmhouse, spread across four bighas, has 50 CCTV cameras. Its boundary wall is 10 feet high and topped with two-foot barbed wire.Yadav has served twice as block pramukh. His wife, Shashi, has also held the post and contested the 2022 Assembly election from Bithoor on a BSP ticket.
Article Summary: BJP Pichhda Morcha state minister Ramesh Yadav was robbed of Rs 50 lakh. Masked men tied his hands and legs at his farmhouse in Kanpur. Police were informed at 1.20 am. The farmhouse, spread across four bighas, has 50 CCTV cameras.

Article Title: Mumbai police rescue abandoned newborn found behind public toilet
Article Text:
Mumbai





: A male infant, about a day old, was found wrapped in an old shirt inside a plastic carrybag behind a public toilet near Jarimari Temple on Andheri-Kurla Road in Sakinaka on Saturday. Sakinaka police registered an FIR against the newborn’s unidentified parents or other relatives under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Section 93, which covers exposure and abandonment of a child aged under 12 years by a parent or carer.Police sub-inspector Namdev Gotpagar, who was on night patrol with three personnel, received a Western Control Room alert at 6.56 am after a caller reported seeing a newborn in the area. “The team is gathering details from the locals and the closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras from the locality to identify the person who dumped the newborn. A local who had gone to the public toilet alerted the police control and the team rescued the infant found behind the toilet,” said a Sakinaka police station officer.Gotpagar and his team reached the spot, where beat officer sub-inspector Mahajan was also present. They heard the infant crying and found him alive inside the bag. “Gotpagar informed night-duty supervisor inspector Nitin Patil and sub-inspector Sachin Ugale.On Patil’s instructions, police took the infant to Sant Mukabai Govt Hospital in Barve Nagar, Ghatkopar West,” said the police.Doctors provided first aid and admitted the child for further treatment and care. The infant was handed over to Dr Sushmita and Dr Pallavi. Woman police constable Shilpa Rathod and police naik Digambar Sapkale were assigned to care for him.
Article Summary: A male infant, about a day old, was found wrapped in an old shirt inside a plastic carrybag behind a public toilet near Jarimari Temple on Andheri-Kurla Road in Sakinaka on Saturday. A local who had gone to the public toilet alerted the police control and the team rescued the infant.

:

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Promoting Christianity does not amount to outraging religious feelings: Bombay HC
Article Text:
Nagpur:





Merely promoting Christianity or insisting on conversion does not mean a person has outraged religious feelings of any class, the Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court held last week. It quashed criminal proceedings against four persons from Amravati, accused of pressuring a couple to convert from Hinduism to Christianity.Justice Mahendra Chandwani observed the allegations against the petitioners, even if taken at face value, did not establish essential ingredients of offences under BNS Section 299 (deliberate and malicious acts to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion). The court also noted the prosecution did not obtain the mandatory govt sanction required to initiate proceedings.The petitioners approached court through counsel HS Chitaley seeking quashing of an FIR registered at Chandur Bazar police station in Amravati and the chargesheet.As per the FIR, the accused allegedly pressured a couple to convert to Christianity between September 1 and November 1, 2025, with offers to pay children’s educational expenses, construct a house and provide permanent employment at a charitable institution in Chandur Bazar.The complaint further alleged the couple was pressured to mention Christianity as their religion in official documents and that their children were influenced by Sunday school sessions.The prosecution contended these offers amounted to inducements for religious conversion. The accused, however, argued the allegations did not disclose any deliberate or malicious act to insult religious beliefs or outrage religious feelings.Examining the allegations, the court held the material indicated, at most, promotion of Christianity or insistence on conversion. It found no material to establish a deliberate and malicious insult to religious beliefs of a class, as required under Section 299 of BNS. Nor was there material to show the petitioners uttered words, made gestures with the intention of wounding any person’s religious feelings, as contemplated under Section 302.The court also noted that prior sanction from the state or central govt was required under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita for prosecution under Section 299, but no such sanction was obtained.Another factor considered by the court was the timing of the alleged acts. The allegations related to a period before Maharashtra’s law prohibiting unlawful religious conversion came into force on August 28, 2026. The court noted that, when the alleged acts took place, there was no law in force prohibiting conversion on the ground of allurements as alleged in the case.Relying on principles laid down by the Supreme Court in State of Haryana versus Bhajan Lal for quashing criminal proceedings, the court allowed the application and quashed the FIR and chargesheet against all four petitioners.
Article Summary: Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court quashes criminal proceedings against four persons from Amravati. Accused of pressuring couple to convert from Hinduism to Christianity. Prosecution did not obtain mandatory govt sanction required to initiate proceedings. The petitioners approached court through counsel HS Chitaley.

Article Title: Lawyers stage protest against alleged misconduct by Delhi police
Article Text:
CJ party members and local lawyers take part in a protest at Sanvidhan Square in Nagpur. Photograph by Aniruddhasingh Dinore.

Nagpur:





Lawyers staged protests outside the District Court and at Samvidhan Chowk against the alleged misconduct by Delhi Police towards senior advocate Shadan Farasat during a peaceful agitation. The protesters condemned the incident, warning that the suppression of lawyers and violation of fundamental rights would not be tolerated.Farasat was detained during a protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Delhi. He alleged that police personnel tore his shirt and threw him into a moving bus. The incident triggered outrage among lawyers in Nagpur, who gathered to raise slogans against police action and criticise Central govt and the administration.Addressing the protesters, advocate Nihalsinh Rathod said fundamental rights were being trampled upon, and the treatment meted out to Farasat reflected the alleged suppression of lawyers in the country.“As lawyers, we are followers of Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar. Babasaheb fought more battles outside the courtroom than inside it. We, too, must now fight along the same path,” Rathod said, calling upon the legal fraternity to stand united in defence of constitutional rights.Several lawyers participated in the demonstration, including former presidents of District Bar Association Kamal Satuja and Roshan Bagde, along with former general secretary Nitin Deshmukh.
Article Summary: Shadan Farasat was detained during a protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Delhi. He alleged that police personnel tore his shirt and threw him into a moving bus. The incident triggered outrage among lawyers in Nagpur, who gathered to raise slogans.
